What this note shows

For every city in the app’s countrymap, two per-city averages are computed:

  • Average Global Spillover — the mean of ev_global (Watson average global spillover per patent family) across all docdbs mapped to the city.
  • Average Spillover to LMICs (excl. China) — the mean of ev_emdenocn across the same docdbs, i.e. the share of those spillovers that land in low- and middle-income countries other than China.

The scatter plot below shows one dot per city. A linear trend line summarises the overall relationship; the largest cities (by patent count) are highlighted, and a hand-picked list of LMIC / mid-tier cities is always labelled regardless of size.

## cities seen: 10,716   (median patents/city: 14, max: 158,279, share_green median: 2.5%)

City selection

To stop the scatter from being dominated by tiny cities with one outlier patent, we keep only those with at least min_patents distinct patent families. The hand-picked label set is always kept, regardless of size — otherwise small LMIC cities (Belém has only ~14 families, Luang Prabang fewer still) would be dropped from the plot and from the abstract-summary section before they can be flagged.

The patent universe here is the “All innovations” view: every docdb in patent_database with a non-null ev_global, no tech filter and no granted-only filter. This matches the HiGGlo “All innovations” tab counts exactly — e.g. Belém: 14 families total, 8 granted.

Scatter: green-tech spillover vs overall spillover

For every city we now have two average global-spillover numbers: the overall mean across all of its docdbs, and the mean restricted to docdbs flagged as Green Technology. Plotting them against each other shows whether a city’s green innovations punch above or below its overall innovation-spillover footprint. The dashed grey line is the 1:1 reference — points above it are cities whose green innovations generate higher-than-average global spillover for that city; points below sit on the other side of the gap.

Cities with zero green docdbs drop out of this view automatically (no green mean to plot). The same big-city anchors and hand-picked LMIC cities are highlighted as in the first scatter.

## OLS:  avg_ev_global_green = 0.2362 + 1.5825 * avg_ev_global
##   R^2 = 0.229, n = 5035 cities
## Cities where green > overall: 3,290 of 5,035 (65.3%)

Patent abstracts and OpenAI summaries

For each highlighted city, we retrieve the top-N patent applications (ranked by ev_global) via the EPO Open Patent Services (OPS) API, then ask gpt-4o-mini to summarise the technological themes that emerge from the titles + abstracts.

This section reuses the EPO/OPS plumbing from insights/patent_cluster_compare.Rmd. Two API keys are required as environment variables; if either is missing the section short-circuits to a warning rather than failing the knit.

Antalya

Open Antalya on HiGGlo →

All fetched patents — 64 with usable title/abstract text from OPS.

Antalya’s patent landscape reveals a diverse technological focus, with notable themes in biotechnology, environmental technology, and medical devices. A significant portion of the patents pertains to biotechnological innovations, particularly in the production of recombinant proteins and plant-derived therapeutic agents, indicating a strong emphasis on health-related applications. Environmental technology is also prominent, with patents addressing water purification systems and energy-efficient methods for utilizing compressed gases, showcasing a commitment to sustainability.

The breadth of technological areas is striking, as Antalya’s patents span from agricultural innovations, such as new cucumber varieties and methods for processing arum seeds, to advanced medical imaging techniques and smart educational tools. This variety suggests a vibrant innovation ecosystem that supports multiple industries.

While specific applicants or institutions are not explicitly mentioned in the abstracts, the focus on plant-based solutions and medical technologies may imply collaboration with agricultural and healthcare research entities. Overall, Antalya’s patent activity reflects a dynamic interplay between health, environment, and technology, positioning the city as a hub for innovative solutions.

Top innovations only — 25 patents with ev_global above the median (median ev_global = 0.000).

Antalya’s patent landscape reveals a strong focus on healthcare technology, environmental solutions, and innovative materials. A significant number of patents pertain to advancements in ophthalmology, particularly methods for fundus photography, indicating a robust interest in improving eye care diagnostics. The diversity of patents suggests a surprising breadth in technological themes, ranging from medical devices to energy-efficient systems and agricultural innovations. This variety reflects a dynamic innovation ecosystem in Antalya, where different sectors are being explored simultaneously.

While specific institutions or applicants are not directly identifiable from the abstracts, the range of technologies implies collaboration among researchers and inventors in fields such as healthcare, environmental science, and materials engineering. This cross-disciplinary approach may foster further advancements and applications in these critical areas.

Firm word cloud per city

Same patents, different angle: pull applicants (<applicant> from the OPS biblio document), explode the ;-joined list into one row per (patent, raw applicant), apply the same heuristic + GPT harmonisation recipe used by patent_cluster_compare.Rmd, and render a per-city word cloud where each word is sized by how many patents mention that canonical firm/institution.

HiGGlo network: per highlighted city

For each of the hand-picked / highlighted cities we capture the HiGGlo citation-network view directly from the live app via headless Chrome (chromote). Same parameters as the URL the user provided for Sofia:

  • City filter: the hand-picked city
  • toflow = ev_global, no firm/tech filter, All countries
  • Gen-0 sampling: Random / Number / 100
  • Edge sampling: Random / Percent / 100
  • add_generations = 2 (one Generate click → gens 1 and 2)

PNGs are cached under .bigdata/innocity/higglo_<city>.png. To force any one of them to refresh, delete the corresponding file and re-knit. The first run captures all of them sequentially in a single chromote session (re-using the warm Shiny server between navigations); budget ~50-70 s per city for a cold first knit, near zero on subsequent knits.

Notes.

  • ev_global is the Watson per-family expected spillover to the whole world; ev_emdenocn is the share of that spillover that lands in LMICs excluding China. Both are docdb-level (one value per family), so per-city averages are unweighted means across the families associated with the city through countrymap.
  • Capital-fallback rows (geocode_missing = TRUE) are dropped before aggregation. Without that, every patent for which no real address survived geocoding would inflate the patent count of the country’s capital.
  • A single docdb may be mapped to multiple cities (e.g. multinational inventor teams). Each city it touches gets credit for the family — there is no proportional split.
  • The abstract-fetch + OpenAI summary section caches both OPS responses and OpenAI completions under .bigdata/innocity/, keyed on the cities and the per-city patent set. Re-knitting the document is free as long as the inputs don’t change. Delete files in that directory to force a refetch / re-summarise.
  • Default scope is the seven hand-picked cities only. To also summarise the 25 biggest cities, edit cities_to_summarise in the summary_helpers chunk — but expect a very long OPS fetch the first time round, since each big city sends max_per_city HTTP calls.
